quotes.quote: Roshan B, Ganda OP, Desilva R, et al, 2011, Homozygous lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) deficiency due to a new loss of function mutation and review of the literature, J Clin Lipidol PMID:22108153

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: NP_000220.1:p.(Met317Arg). The papers describe the disease as autosomal recessive and caused by loss of LCAT function; the review also notes an intermediate (co-dominant) biochemical phenotype in heterozygous carriers.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.

carriers of one mutant LCAT allele show an intermediate biochemical phenotype between homozygous carriers and controls, suggesting that the disease, which is reported as recessive, is indeed co-dominant for the biochemical phenotype.

concerns: The variant appears only in a summary row of a systematic review table (34256778) without a case description; data are second-hand from the cited case report.
Zygosity is not in the table; 'homozygous' is only in the title of the cited reference [93].
The review's REF numbers in Table 1 do not always match its reference list (e.g. the Korean and Australian rows); check that reference [93] is the source of this row.
Same nucleotide as candidate G-lcat-008 (c.950T>C), a different substitution; do not merge.
notes_for_panel: Lebanese male with FLD (REF 93, 'CR & R'). Reference [93] in the review's list is Roshan et al. 2011, 'Homozygous ... LCAT deficiency due to a new loss of function mutation and review of the literature', which matches the row's study type, but zygosity is not given in the table itself. Note the different variant at the same nucleotide: candidate G-lcat-008 is c.950T>C (Met317Thr, legacy Met293Thr) in a Japanese patient (25984174).
